title: Shared site failure raised minimum averaging variance in models of eight worm brain maps
abstract: We tested how polyadic chemical sites affect a common source signal averaged across its targets. Eight public C. elegans brain maps supplied site membership in a fixed 162-neuron panel. Each site had an independent survival event, shared by its listed targets. Independent incidence events gave a reference with the same target means and marginal variances. Across maps, median equal-weight variance ratios were 1.58 to 2.04. After optimal nonnegative target weighting, median variance ratios against the independent optimum were 1.90 to 2.17. All ratios cancel the common survival probability. Partial-sharing checks reduced the equal-weight cost as expected. These are exact covariance calculations under assumed failures, not measured noise or neural decoding results. We provide source-level results, site membership, decoder weights, solver bounds, simulations and raw file hashes.

display.caption: Median variance ratios for each map under the stated failure model. The left panel uses equal target weights. The right panel compares optimal nonnegative weights with the independent-contact optimum. Lines join different animals and do not show longitudinal change.

citations.reason: Primary site-level chemical connectome data across development.
Shared responses at worm neuromuscular polyadic sites motivate the model; this evidence does not establish shared failures in the brain.
Reuses its verified 162-cell pre-hatching brain panel and panel provenance. No analysis code or outcome tables reused.
